result.summary: Full property inventory of the FDAT-relevant LCM classes from MasterLCModel.xml (model version 7000072), with answers to the four questions. Key results: (1) A Text CAN hold many media files: Text.MediaFiles (OA, CmMediaContainer) -> CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs (OC, CmMediaURI); each CmMediaURI stores a single Unicode string 'MediaURI' (a media-fragment URI, ELAN placeholder) plus the container's Unicode 'OffsetType' - it does NOT reference a CmFile and FLEx only writes it from BIRD/ELAN import. The separate LinkedFiles machinery (CmFile.InternalPath/OriginalPath, owned by CmFolder under LangProject.Media/Pictures/FilePathsInTsStrings) is what FLExBridge syncs (LinkedFiles/AudioVisual|Others|Pictures/**.*). (2) Free/rich-text slots: Text.Source (MultiString), Text.Abbreviation (MultiUnicode), inherited Name (MultiUnicode) and Description (MultiString); StText has none itself; StTxtPara.Contents/Label (String); Segment.FreeTranslation/LiteralTranslation (MultiString), Reference (String), BeginTimeOffset/EndTimeOffset (Unicode), Notes (OS Note, Note.Content MultiString); ConstChartRow.Notes and .Label (String); CmPossibility.Name/Abbreviation (MultiUnicode), Description (MultiString), Discussion (OA StText), HelpId (Unicode); RnGenericRec.Title (String) plus many OA StText fields. (3) Possibility references: Text.Genres (RC), ConstituentChartCellPart.Column (RA), ConstChartTag.Tag (RA), TextTag.Tag (RA), DsChart.Template (RA), CmPossibility.Restrictions (RC)/Confidence (RA)/Status (RA), Segment.Speaker (RA CmPerson), RnGenericRec.Confidence/Restrictions/PhraseTags/TimeOfEvent/Type/Status, CmTranslation.Type, and LCM custom ReferenceAtomic/ReferenceCollection fields with DstCls=CmPossibility. (4) Open fields: ConstChartRow has Notes(String)+Label(String); Segment has Notes(OS Note), Reference(String), and is one of the six classes FLEx's UI allows custom fields on; StTxtPara has Label(String, unused); CmPossibility has Description, Discussion(StText), HelpId, plus ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor/UnderStyle/Hidden integers/booleans usable for colour. The model XML has NO attribute marking custom-field-capable classes; LCM's AddCustomField accepts any model class; FLEx's Add Custom Field dialog restricts the UI to LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm, Segment, RnGenericRec.

findings.implication: Per-text FDAT anchors exist: Text.Description (MultiString, rich text) and Text.Source are free text; MediaFiles is a single container but it owns a collection, so 'more than one media file' is possible (see next finding). Text is unowned (owner="none"), so it is a top-level object in the FLExBridge TextCorpus files.

findings.claim: A Text CAN hold more than one media/linked file, via Text.MediaFiles (OA, one CmMediaContainer) -> CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs (owning COLLECTION of CmMediaURI). CmMediaContainer stores only OffsetType (Unicode) plus the collection; CmMediaURI stores only a single Unicode string 'MediaURI' described as 'the location and offset of the media file, this should be a subset of the MediaFragment specification'. Neither class references a CmFile or the LinkedFiles folder; both are documented as 'Currently a placeholder for ELAN data, not modifiable or viewable in flex as of Nov 2011'.
findings.evidence: CmMediaURI (num 72): <basic num="1" id="MediaURI" sig="Unicode"> 'The location and offset of the media file, this should be a subset of the MediaFragment specification. see http://www.w3.org/2008/WebVideo/Fragments/WD-media-fragments-spec/'. CmMediaContainer (num 73): 'This class collects any number of MediaURIs and provides an offset type' — <basic num="1" id="OffsetType" sig="Unicode"/> <owning num="2" id="MediaURIs" card="col" sig="CmMediaURI"/>. Segment.MediaURI (rel atomic CmMediaURI, 'This references a media file in the interlinear text').
findings.implication: The owner's 'linked file of the text' idea maps to CmMediaURI, which is just a URI string - it does not copy anything into LinkedFiles, is not shown/edited in FLEx, and FLEx code only writes it during BIRD/ELAN (.flextext) import (BIRDInterlinearImporter.cs:1372-1392 creates the container and adds ICmMediaURI objects by GUID; InterlinearExporter.cs:884-889 exports them). An FDAT JSON could be pointed at by an extra CmMediaURI (MediaURI = relative path under LinkedFiles/Others), but the file itself must be placed in LinkedFiles/Others (or AudioVisual) for FLExBridge to sync it (FlexFolderSystem.cs:61-63 includes only LinkedFiles/AudioVisual, Others, Pictures). InterlinVc.cs:1138 and InterlinDocForAnalysis.cs:2237 read segment.MediaURIRA?.MediaURI for playback, so a Segment pointing at a JSON would be nonsense; a text-level URI not referenced by any Segment is inert. INFERRED: risk that a future FLEx version tries to open all MediaURIs as audio.

Per-row FDAT data (salience band, custom columns) therefore needs a side structure keyed by the ConstChartRow GUID (e.g. a custom field on the Segment(s) the row covers, a TextTag, or entries in an FDAT-owned list/file).

findings.claim: The model XML has no attribute or list marking which classes may carry custom fields: the <class> element's XSD attributes are only num, id, abbr, abstract, base, depth, singleton, owner, generateBasicCreateMethod. LCM's LcmMetaDataCache.AddCustomField(className, ...) accepts ANY class name in the model (it only checks CheckClid(className), rejects a name clash with a non-custom field, and allocates flid = clid*1000+500+n). The restriction to specific classes is purely in FLEx's UI: AddCustomFieldDlg offers LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm (Lexicon), Segment (Interlinear), RnGenericRec (Notebook), with types SingleLineText (String or MultiUnicode), MultiparagraphText (OwningAtomic StText), Number (Integer), Date (GenDate), ListRefAtomic/ListRefCollection (ReferenceAtomic/ReferenceCollection with DstCls=CmPossibility and a ListRootId).
findings.evidence: MasterLCModel.xsd:26-32 lists class attributes abbr, abstract, base, depth, singleton, owner, generateBasicCreateMethod (no custom-field flag; grep -i custom in MasterLCModel.xml matches only CmCustomItem and comments). LcmMetaDataCache.cs:920-965: 'CheckClid(className); ... if (m_nameToFlid.TryGetValue(MakeFlidKey(clid, fieldName), out flid) && !IsCustom(flid)) throw ...; flid = (clid*1000) + 500;'. AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:111-125: LexEntryTags/LexSenseTags/LexExampleSentenceTags/MoFormTags; 'case LocationType.Interlinear: ... SegmentTags.kClassId, "Segment"'; RnGenericRecTags. AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:402-434 type mapping.
findings.implication: Technically LCM/flexlibs could add a custom field to ConstChartRow or Text, but FLEx's UI, its BasicCustomPropertyFixer (comment at AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:112,123), FLExBridge's custom-property file handling, and the layout/config system are only exercised for the six UI classes. INFERRED: to stay safe FDAT should confine custom fields to Segment (per clause/row anchor) and RnGenericRec (per text), and use lists/TextTags/Description fields for the rest.

findings.claim: FLExBridge learns custom properties from a single project-level file FLExProject.CustomProperties (<AdditionalFields><CustomField class=... name=...>) and registers them on the named class in its own MetadataCache via AddCustomPropInfo(className, FdoPropertyInfo); the folder configuration includes that file, **.list, **.style, LinkedFiles/AudioVisual|Others|Pictures/**.*, Linguistics/TextCorpus/*.textincorpus and Linguistics/Discourse/<DiscourseChartFilename>, and excludes **.xml, **.flextext, **.zip and video extensions.
findings.evidence: MetadataCache.cs:447-452 'internal void AddCustomPropInfo(string className, FdoPropertyInfo propInfo) { ... _classes[className].AddProperty(propInfo); }'; :492-503 reads FlexBridgeConstants.CustomPropertiesFilename, iterates CustomField elements, className = attribute Class. FlexFolderSystem.cs:34 ExcludePatterns '**.xml'; :24 '**.flextext'; :45 AddExcludedVideoExtensions; :48 'FLExProject.CustomProperties'; :57-58 '**.list', '**.style'; :61-63 LinkedFiles/AudioVisual, Others, Pictures '**.*'; :75 Linguistics/TextCorpus/*.textincorpus; :77 Linguistics/Discourse/DiscourseChartFilename.

result.summary: FLEx's Add Custom Field dialog (Src/xWorks/AddCustomFieldDlg.cs) offers exactly six classes, chosen by area: Lexicon -> LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm ("Allomorph"); Notebook -> RnGenericRec ("Record"); Texts & Words -> Segment. Value types offered: Single-line text (String or MultiUnicode depending on WS selector), Multiparagraph text (OwningAtomic StText), List reference single (ReferenceAtomic CmPossibility) and multiple (ReferenceCollection CmPossibility), Date (GenDate), Number (Integer) - and Segment gets only Single-line text. Text, Wordform, ConstChartRow, CmPossibility, TextTag etc. are NOT offered. However, LCM itself (IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.AddCustomField / LcmMetaDataCache.AddCustomField) accepts ANY class name in the model and any CellarPropertyType; the flid is clid*1000+500+n, and CmObject serialises/deserialises <Custom name=..> elements for Guid, Boolean, Integer, GenDate, Time, Unicode, String, Binary, OwningAtomic/ReferenceAtomic, MultiString/MultiUnicode and all four vector types, on any class. Definitions persist in the .fwdata <AdditionalFields><CustomField class= name= type= destclass= wsSelector= helpString= listRoot= label=/> header; values persist as <Custom name="X"> children of the object's <rt> element. FLExBridge splits the definitions into FLExProject.CustomProperties (merged atomically per class+name; explicitly included first in the Chorus folder config), loads them into its own MetadataCache before validating/merging any data file (skipping unknown class names), keys <Custom> elements by "Custom_<class>_<name>", validates custom properties generically via CmObjectValidator (including inside Linguistics/Discourse/Charting.discourse), and writes values back into the .fwdata on Receive. So custom fields on classes like ConstChartRow or ConstChartWordGroup are technically supported end-to-end by LCM and FLExBridge - but (a) FLEx's dialog will not show or let users delete them (it filters to its combo classes), (b) the FLEx DataTree auto-displays custom fields only for objects edited in a data-entry view (not charts), (c) the FixData BasicCustomPropertyFixer only knows MoForm's subclasses, so an Integer/GenDate custom field on an ABSTRACT class with subclasses (e.g. ConstituentChartCellPart) could leave merged new objects missing the required value element; value-type fields on concrete leaf classes are fine, and reference/string/StText fields are optional elements and unaffected; (d) FLEx itself warns that Send/Receive of custom-field definition CHANGES is fragile and recommends one designated person add fields; (e) FLEx refuses to add fields when another app shares the project. flexlibs offers GetFieldID/GetCustomFieldValue/LexiconSetFieldText/LexiconSetFieldInteger/LexiconSetListField* which take any hvo/object and flid (they are not restricted to lexicon classes despite the names) but supports only String, MultiUnicode/MultiString, Integer and CmPossibility references; it has no wrapper to create custom fields (must call the LCM MDC AddCustomField via pythonnet directly, inside a UOW). Custom Segment/StText/list/reference fields could each carry FDAT data, but the mirror-image design choice remains: a custom field on ConstChartRow is invisible in FLEx UI yet fully synced, whereas a custom field on Segment is user-visible in the interlinear Configure dialog.

result.summary: Linked files are a workable but narrow place for an FDAT JSON. Send/Receive (FLExBridge on Chorus/Mercurial) includes exactly three LinkedFiles subfolders of the project folder — LinkedFiles/AudioVisual, LinkedFiles/Others, LinkedFiles/Pictures (plus SupportingFiles) — via explicit include patterns; nothing else in the project folder is synced unless explicitly listed. ".json" is not excluded (only **.xml, **.zip, and video/backup/temp extensions are), so <project>/LinkedFiles/Others/fdat/<something>.json will be committed and pushed. Constraints that the design depends on: (1) the hg repo root is the folder of the .fwdata file, so the file only syncs when LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir is the default in-project LinkedFiles folder (a project whose LinkedFiles were relocated to a shared drive syncs none of them); (2) Chorus's LargeFileFilter caps unknown extensions such as .json at 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes; images/audio get 10 MiB, .txt/.lift unlimited) — an oversized file is excluded and, if already tracked, 'forgotten' with only a warning in the S/R log; (3) no handler merges .json: FlexBridge's handler declines it and Chorus falls to DefaultFileTypeHandler, which records an 'unmergable file type' conflict note and keeps the merging machine's copy ('WeWin'), i.e. whole-file, last-merger-wins, other side's edits silently dropped from the working copy. At the model level, no LCM property is needed for the file to sync; the properties that can point at a linked file are CmFile.InternalPath (relative to LinkedFilesRootDir, owned in CmFolders under LangProject.Pictures/Media/FilePathsInTsStrings and referenced by CmPicture.PictureFile and CmMedia.MediaFile), kodtExternalPathName runs in TsStrings ('Insert Link to File', which copies the file into LinkedFiles/Others and registers a CmFile), and CmMediaURI.MediaURI (a raw URI string, one Text.MediaFiles container holding any number of CmMediaURIs, created only by FLExText import, shown read-only as static text in the Text's Info tab 'Media' field, played only when a Segment references it and the URI is an existing local file; no type validation). A CmMediaURI pointing at a .json therefore 'works' (FLEx displays the path, never opens it), but it conflates FDAT data with ELAN media metadata that gets exported/re-imported with the text; a CmFile in a dedicated CmFolder under LangProject.Media, or simply no pointer at all, is cleaner. FLEx backup includes everything under an in-project LinkedFiles folder when 'include linked files' is checked, and only CmFile-registered files when LinkedFiles is elsewhere.

findings.claim: FLExBridge syncs only three LinkedFiles subfolders, by explicit include pattern: LinkedFiles/AudioVisual/**.*, LinkedFiles/Others/**.*, LinkedFiles/Pictures/**.* (plus SupportingFiles/**.*). A file anywhere else in the project folder (project root, ConfigurationSettings, LinkedFiles/<other subfolder>) is not synced.

findings.implication: An FDAT JSON must live under <project>/LinkedFiles/Others (or AudioVisual/Pictures) to be carried by Send/Receive. A subfolder such as LinkedFiles/Others/fdat/ is covered because the pattern is **.* (Mercurial '**' matches across directory separators — inferred from hg glob semantics, not from FLExBridge code).

findings.claim: Chorus runs LargeFileFilter before every commit. The maximum size for a file is looked up by extension from the installed file-type handlers; an extension no handler claims (which includes 'json') gets the default of exactly 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes). Images (bmp, jpg, jpeg, gif, png, tif, tiff, ico, wmf, pcx, cgm) and audio (wav, snd, au, aif, aifc, aiff, wma, mp3, webm) get 10 MiB; .txt and .lift are unlimited; FlexBridge's own split-file extensions are unlimited (int.MaxValue). The '10 MB' mentioned in the 2022 comment is implemented only in the image/audio handlers, not in the default.
findings.evidence: LargeFileFilter: 'public static uint Megabyte => 1048576;' ... 'if (!extensionToMaximumSize.TryGetValue(extension, out maxForExtension)) { maxForExtension = Megabyte; }'. Synchronizer.Commit: 'string tooLargeFilesMessage = LargeFileFilter.FilterFiles(Repository, _project, _handlers);'. DefaultFileTypeHandler.MaximumFileSize returns LargeFileFilter.Megabyte and GetExtensionsOfKnownTextFileTypes yields nothing; ImageFileTypeHandler/AudioFileTypeHandler return 'LargeFileFilter.Megabyte * 10'; TextFileTypeHandler ('txt') and LiftFileHandler return UInt32.MaxValue. FlexBridge: 'uint IChorusFileTypeHandler.MaximumFileSize => int.MaxValue;' with GetExtensionsOfKnownTextFileTypes = '_handlers.Select(handlerStrategy => handlerStrategy.Extension)' (its FLEx split-file extensions).
findings.implication: An FDAT .json is hard-capped at 1 MiB per file. Keep one file per chart (or per text), keep it compact (no pretty-printing, no embedded chart data), and have FDAT refuse to write past ~900 KB. Naming the file .txt would remove the cap (and change merge behaviour, see below).

findings.claim: An oversized file is not an error: Chorus appends its path to ExcludePatterns, and if the file is already tracked (status M or A) it runs 'hg forget' on it, so it stops being versioned; the user only gets a warning line in the Send/Receive progress log.
findings.evidence: 'File '{0}' is too large to include in the Send/Receive system. It is {1}, but the maximum allowed is {2}. The file is at {3}.' / 'has grown too large ...'; 'configuration.ExcludePatterns.Add(shortPathname); if (forgetItIfTooLarge) repository.ForgetFile(shortPathname);' with forgetItIfTooLarge = true for status "M" and "A". Synchronizer: 'We're sorry, but the Send/Receive system can't handle large files. The following files won't be stored or shared ...' written via _progress.WriteWarning.
findings.implication: If the FDAT JSON grows past 1 MiB, colleagues silently stop receiving updates (they keep the last small version). FDAT must enforce the limit itself and surface it in its UI.

findings.claim: No handler can merge a .json: FlexBridge's single IChorusFileTypeHandler answers CanMergeFile/CanDiffFile via CanValidateFile, which dispatches on extension to its per-extension strategies and falls to UnknownFileTypeHandlerStrategy (CanValidateFile returns false); Chorus's own handlers claim only .txt, .lift, images, audio, etc. ChorusMerge therefore uses DefaultFileTypeHandler.

'var handler = GetHandlerFromExtension(extension.Substring(1)); return handler.CanValidateFile(pathToFile);' with 'GetHandlerFromExtension ... ?? _unknownFileTypeHandler'; UnknownFileTypeHandlerStrategy.CanValidateFile 'return false;'. Chorus TextFileTypeHandler.CanMergeFile: 'return (Path.GetExtension(pathToFile) == ".txt");'. ChorusFileTypeHandlerCollection.GetHandlerForMerging: 'return handler ?? new DefaultFileTypeHandler();'. ChorusMerge Program: 'var handler = handlers.GetHandlerForMerging(order.pathToOurs); ... handler.Do3WayMerge(order);'.
findings.implication: There is no element-level or line-level merge for the FDAT JSON; conflict resolution is whole-file (next finding).

findings.claim: When both sides changed a .json, DefaultFileTypeHandler.Do3WayMerge records an UnmergableFileTypeConflict in the merge listener (written to a .NewChorusNotes file next to the data) and, because Chorus always runs the merge in 'WeWin' mode, leaves the merging machine's own version in place; the other user's version is only in Mercurial history. In 'TheyWin' mode it would copy theirs over ours; there is no combining.
findings.evidence: DefaultFileTypeHandler.Do3WayMerge: 'XmlMergeService.AddConflictToListener(mergeOrder.EventListener, new UnmergableFileTypeConflict(mergeOrder.MergeSituation)); switch (...ConflictHandlingMode) { default: // just leave our file there ... case WeWin: break; case TheyWin: File.Copy(mergeOrder.pathToTheirs, mergeOrder.pathToOurs, true); }'. Synchronizer: 'Go with WeWin, since that is the default ... using (new ShortTermEnvironmentalVariable(MergeOrder.kConflictHandlingModeEnvVarName, MergeOrder.ConflictHandlingModeChoices.WeWin.ToString()))'; MergeSituation.CreateFromEnvironmentVariables defaults 'var mode = MergeOrder.ConflictHandlingModeChoices.WeWin;'. ChorusMerge Program: 'using (var xmlListener = new ChorusNotesMergeEventListener(order.pathToOurs + ".NewChorusNotes"))'.
findings.implication: Two linguists annotating the same chart between syncs lose one side's work (the side that did not perform the merge). Mitigations: one file per chart (conflicts only when the same chart is edited), or keep frequently-edited data in LCM objects, or have FDAT detect the ChorusNotes conflict record. Same whole-file semantics as the custom-field-string option in PLAN.md §5, but with the extra 1 MiB cap and no FLEx visibility.

findings.claim: Naming the file with a .txt extension changes both constraints: Chorus's TextFileTypeHandler claims .txt with no size limit and merges it line-by-line with diff3 (Windows: bundled diff3.exe), but it throws on an overlapping-line conflict; ChorusMerge then exits with code 1 ('ChorusMerge Error'), and what Mercurial/Chorus does with the file after a failed merge tool is not established here.
findings.evidence: TextFileTypeHandler: CanMergeFile '== ".txt"'; Do3WayMerge calls GetRawMerge via diff3 '-m'; RunProcess: 'if(result.ExitCode == 1) throw new ApplicationException("Could not merge text files without conflict: " ...'; MaximumFileSize 'return UInt32.MaxValue;'; '_diff3Exe = Platform.IsWindows ? "diff3/bin/diff3.exe" : "diff3"'. Program.cs catch: 'ErrorWriter.WriteLine("ChorusMerge Error: " + e.Message); ... return 1;'.
findings.implication: A line-oriented JSON (one record per line, sorted by GUID) saved as .txt would auto-merge non-overlapping edits by different users and lift the 1 MiB cap, but the conflict path is unverified and risky; only consider after a two-machine test. FlexBridge's handler declines .txt too (unknown extension), so Chorus's text handler is the one that runs — inferred from MEF FirstOrDefault over both handler sets.

findings.claim: The synced FDAT file needs no LCM object at all: Send/Receive adds files purely by location/pattern ('hg add -I ... -X ...'), and deletions in the working directory are recorded and propagated ('hg rm -A').

CmFile objects are owned by CmFolder.Files; LangProject owns folder collections Pictures ('Local Pictures'), Media ('Local Media') and one FilePathsInTsStrings folder ('File paths in TsStrings'). CmFile is referenced by CmPicture.PictureFile and CmMedia.MediaFile (CmMedia owned by LexPronunciation.MediaFiles), and owned directly by ScrImportSFFiles.Files.

A .json URI is never validated or opened by FLEx. Not harmful, but it misuses an ELAN-media slot; prefer no pointer or a CmFile in a dedicated folder.

MediaURI values are absolute URIs in practice, so a synced pointer would show a colleague the original author's path.

findings.claim: FLEx's project backup includes every file under LinkedFiles when the folder is inside the project folder and 'include linked files' is selected; if LinkedFiles is elsewhere, only files with a CmFile object in LangProject.Media/Pictures/FilePathsInTsStrings folders are backed up.

'If the LinkedFiles folder is located inside the project folder, return all the files under this folder. result.summary: Text tags (TextTag) and possibility lists are viable, Send/Receive-safe anchors for FDAT, with concrete constraints. TextTag is a small class owned by StText.Tags that references BeginSegment/EndSegment (Segment objects) plus integer analysis indices and one CmPossibility Tag; LCM's TextTagFactory.CreateOnText and the FLEx tagging UI both create them, tags of different tag types may overlap freely (same-type overlaps are replaced), and tags may span segment boundaries (tests exercise 2-segment tags, but code comments and a NotImplementedException show 3+-segment spans are only partially supported). FLEx displays a tag as the possibility's Abbreviation in brackets on its own row under the word bundles - one row per top-level "tag type" - with no colour. The tag list is LangProject.TextMarkupTags, a strict two-level structure (tag types -> tags) enforced by the Lists-area tree handler; FLEx refuses to delete any tag possibility that a TextTag references, or any IsProtected possibility, so a 'Salience' tag type with band sub-tags fits FLEx's own model exactly and is protected by FLEx's own rules. CmPossibility carries ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor/UnderStyle/Hidden integer fields (BGR-encoded, legacy 'overlay' feature) that no FLEx UI in the examined code renders and that the Lists editor explicitly hides, so FDAT can store colours there invisibly and they round-trip through FLExBridge with the list. Custom lists are unowned CmPossibilityLists whose items are CmCustomItem (created via ICmPossibilityListFactory.CreateUnowned, identified by Owner==null, must have a project-unique Name); FLExBridge writes each one to General/UserDefinedLists/UserList-<guid>.list, the TextMarkupTags list to Linguistics/TextCorpus/TextMarkupTags.list, and chart markers to Linguistics/Discourse, all covered by the '**.list' include pattern and 3-way merged. Chart markers (ConstChartTag.Tag) are possibilities in DsDiscourseData.ChartMarkers displayed by Abbreviation, giving stable GUID anchors for FDAT marker styling. Caveats: TextTag anchors to segment+word, not to ConstChartRow, so row salience stored as a TextTag duplicates the row's extent; LCM's AnalysisAdjuster deletes tags whose words are edited away; FLEx's Add Custom Field dialog does not offer CmPossibility/CmCustomItem/ConstChartRow as hosts (only LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm, Segment, RnGenericRec); flexlibs offers only a read helper (UnpackNestedPossibilityList), so FDAT would call LCM factories directly.

findings.claim: TextTag is a CmObject with exactly five properties: BeginSegment and EndSegment (atomic references to Segment), BeginAnalysisIndex and EndAnalysisIndex (integers indexing Segment.Analyses), and Tag (atomic reference to CmPossibility); it is owned in StText.Tags (owning collection).

The span is addressed by Segment GUID + integer index (not by analysis GUID), the same addressing ConstChartWordGroup uses, so a chart row's extent and a salience tag can be expressed identically.
